args.title: Enhancing Patent Retrieval using Text and Knowledge Graph Embeddings: A Technical Note
args.summary:
Proposes retrieving patents relevant to an initial set of patents by representing multiple facets of a patent, text, citation, and inventor, in a single embedding rather than text alone. Sentence-BERT encodes titles and abstracts; TransE is trained separately on the citation knowledge graph and the inventor knowledge graph; a classification task selects concatenation of text+citation+inventor as the preferred combined representation. Retrieval ranks/associates target patents via mean cosine similarity over multiple initial patents. Applied to two curated sets, a product family and an inventor's portfolio, with qualitative design-inspiration evaluation rather than standard IR benchmarking (no MAP/NDCG). Retrieved patents surface distant yet in-domain concepts useful for design inspiration, though citation-sharing bias limits discovery of distant in-domain patents that do not share citations.

key_facts: Combines Sentence-BERT text embeddings with TransE embeddings trained separately on a citation knowledge graph and an inventor knowledge graph.
Concatenation of text, citation, and inventor embeddings is selected as the preferred patent representation via a classification task.
Retrieval ranks target patents by mean cosine similarity computed over multiple initial (query) patents.
Evaluated qualitatively on two curated sets (a product family and an inventor's portfolio); no standard IR benchmark, no MAP/NDCG reported.
Citation-sharing and original-search mechanisms bias the retrieved neighborhood; distant in-domain concepts can be missed when patents do not share citations.
